def-it-general-mutual-information:
## Definition

Assume AC. Let $X,Y$ be random elements with standard-Borel value spaces $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ and $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)$, and let $P_{XY}$, $P_X$, and $P_Y$ be their joint and marginal probability laws. The product law $P_X\otimes P_Y$ exists by [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]]. Define the mutual information in nats by

$$I_{\mathrm{nat}}(X;Y):=D(P_{XY}\|P_X\otimes P_Y)\in[0,+\infty],$$

where $D$ is the directional Kullback–Leibler divergence of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. This definition remains meaningful when one or both laws have no Lebesgue density and does not subtract differential entropies that may be infinite.
def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-bloc:
## Definition

Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ and $(\widehat{\mathcal X},\widehat{\mathcal A})$ be measurable spaces, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,+\infty]$ be a measurable single-letter distortion. For a positive integer $n$, define the normalized additive block distortion by

$$d_n(x^n,\widehat x^n):=\frac1n\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}d(x_i,\widehat x_i).$$

When the alphabets are finite and $d$ is finite-valued, define $d_{\max}:=\max_{x,\widehat x}d(x,\widehat x)$. Expected distortion is $\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)$; the excess-distortion probability at threshold $D$ is $\mathbb P(d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)>D)$. These are distinct criteria: one is an expectation and the other is a tail probability.
lem-it-finite-vector-gaussian-water-leve:
## Statement

Let $m\ge1$, let $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m\ge0$, and for $0\le\delta_i\le\lambda_i$ put

$$\phi_i(\delta_i):=\begin{cases}\frac12\log_2(\lambda_i/\delta_i),&\lambda_i>0,\ 0<\delta_i\le\lambda_i,\\+\infty,&\lambda_i>0,\ \delta_i=0,\\0,&\lambda_i=0,\ \delta_i=0.\end{cases}$$

For a total distortion budget $D\ge0$, minimize $\sum_i\phi_i(\delta_i)$ subject to $\sum_i\delta_i\le D$ and $0\le\delta_i\le\lambda_i$. If $0<D<\sum_i\lambda_i$, there is a unique $\theta\in(0,\max_i\lambda_i)$ satisfying

$$\sum_i\min(\lambda_i,\theta)=D,$$

and the minimum is

$$\frac12\sum_i\log_2^+(\lambda_i/\theta),\qquad \delta_i^*=\min(\lambda_i,\theta),$$

where $\log_2^+(u):=\max(0,\log_2 u)$. If $D=0$, the minimum is $+\infty$ when some $\lambda_i>0$ and is $0$ when all $\lambda_i=0$. If $D\ge\sum_i\lambda_i$, the minimum is $0$.
def-it-general-rate-distortion-function:
## Definition

Assume AC. Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $P_X$ be a probability law on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable. A feasible joint law, or coupling, is a probability measure $\pi$ on $\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}$ whose $\mathcal X$-marginal is $P_X$. Define

$$R_{\mathrm{std}}(D):=\inf_{\substack{\pi_{\mathcal X}=P_X\\ \int d\,d\pi\le D}}\frac{D(\pi\|P_X\otimes\pi_{\widehat{\mathcal X}})}{\ln2}=\inf_{\substack{\pi_{\mathcal X}=P_X\\ \int d\,d\pi\le D}}\frac{I_{\mathrm{nat}}(X;\widehat X)}{\ln2}.$$

The infimum of an empty feasible set is $+\infty$. Values are in bits. This definition makes no general existence or attainment claim and supplies no operational coding theorem for arbitrary standard-Borel alphabets.
def-it-operational-rate-distortion-funct:
## Definition

Let $X_0,X_1,\ldots$ be a source over a finite alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite, and let $d$ be finite-valued. An $n$-block fixed-length code with $M_n$ messages is a deterministic encoder $f_n:\mathcal X^n\to[M_n]$ and decoder $g_n:[M_n]\to\widehat{\mathcal X}^{\,n}$; its reconstruction is $\widehat X^n=g_n(f_n(X^n))$, its block distortion is [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]], and its rate is $n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ bits per source symbol.

Define the expected-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{avg}}(D)$ as the infimum of $\limsup_n n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ over code sequences satisfying $\limsup_n\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)\le D$. Define the positive-slack excess-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{slack}}(D)$ by the same rate infimum over code sequences satisfying

$$\text{for every }\varepsilon>0,\qquad \mathbb P\!\left(d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)>D+\varepsilon\right)\longrightarrow0.$$

The expected and positive-slack excess criteria are separate definitions. An exact-threshold condition $\mathbb P(d_n>D)\to0$ is not part of either definition.
lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-at:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite sets, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. Put
$$
D_{\min}:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p(x)\min_{\hat x\in\widehat{\mathcal X}}d(x,\hat x).
$$
For every $D\ge0$, the feasible stochastic channels $W(\hat x\mid x)$ satisfying $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)\le D$ form a nonempty set exactly when $D\ge D_{\min}$. Whenever nonempty, mutual information in bits attains its minimum over this set.
def-it-information-rate-distortion-funct:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite alphabets, let $p$ be a pmf on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. A test channel is a stochastic matrix $W(\hat x\mid x)$, and its expected single-letter distortion is $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)$, with block distortion as in [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]]. Put $D_{\min}=\sum_xp(x)\min_{\hat x}d(x,\hat x)$. Define, in bits,
$$
R_{p,d}(D):=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\min_{W:\,\mathbb E d(X,\hat X)\le D} I(X;\hat X),&D\ge D_{\min},\\[4pt]+\infty,&D<D_{\min}. \end{cases}
$$
The minimum exists by [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]]. Values are not operational code rates; the finite memoryless coding theorem is a separate claim.
def-it-stationary-finite-block-informati:
## Definition

Let $(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a stationary source on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be a bounded finite-valued distortion. For $n\ge1$ and $D\ge0$, define
$$
R_n(D):=\frac1n\min_{W_n:\,\mathbb E d_n(X_0^{n-1},\widehat X_0^{n-1})\le D} I(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})\quad\text{bits/symbol},
$$
with value $+\infty$ when the constraint is infeasible. The minimum is attained whenever feasible by [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]] applied to the block alphabets. Put
$$
D_{\min}:=\mathbb E\min_{\hat x\in\widehat{\mathcal X}}d(X_0,\hat x),\qquad D_{\rm c}:=\min_{\hat x\in\widehat{\mathcal X}}\mathbb E d(X_0,\hat x),\qquad R_{\rm block}(D):=\inf_{n\ge1}R_n(D).
$$
The stationary-ergodic process information rate-distortion quantity is
$$
R_{\rm erg}(D):=\inf \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n I(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1}),
$$
where the infimum ranges over jointly stationary ergodic pairs of finite-alphabet processes with the given source marginal and $\mathbb E d(X_0,\widehat X_0)\le D$; an empty infimum is $+\infty$. The block-limit lemma proves $R_n(D)\to R_{\rm block}(D)$, convexity, and right continuity at $D_{\min}$.
lem-it-gaussian-reference-kernel-informa:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $X\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma^2>0$, let $Y$ be any real-valued reconstruction jointly distributed with $X$, and suppose $0<D<\sigma^2$ and $\delta:=\mathbb E(X-Y)^2\le D$. Then

$$I_{\mathrm{nat}}(X;Y)\ge\frac12\ln\frac{\sigma^2}{D}.$$

No density for $Y$, conditional differential entropy, or subtraction of potentially infinite entropies is assumed.
lem-it-rate-distortion-convexity-and-mon:
## Statement

Let the source and reproduction alphabets be finite nonempty sets and let the distortion be finite-valued and nonnegative. The finite-alphabet information rate-distortion function $R(D)$ of [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]] is finite and nonincreasing on $[D_{\min},\infty)$, convex there, zero for $D\ge D_{\rm c}:=\min_{\hat x}\mathbb E d(X,\hat x)$, and right-continuous at every feasible distortion, including $D_{\min}$.
thm-it-binary-hamming-rate-distortion:
## Statement

Let $X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)$, $0\le p\le1$, and let the reproduction alphabet be $\{0,1\}$ with Hamming distortion $d(x,\hat x)=\mathbf1_{\{x\ne\hat x\}}$. Write $p_0:=\min(p,1-p)$ and
$$
h_2(u):=-u\log_2u-(1-u)\log_2(1-u),\qquad 0\log_20:=0.
$$
Then the finite-alphabet information rate-distortion function is
$$
R(D)=\begin{cases}h_2(p)-h_2(D),&0\le D\le p_0,\\0,&D\ge p_0.\end{cases}
$$
alg-it-finite-alphabet-blahut-arimoto:
## Definition

Let $p_1,\ldots,p_m>0$ be source probabilities summing to one, let $d_{ij}\ge0$ be finite distortions on a nonempty finite reproduction alphabet $[n]$, and let $\beta\ge0$ be finite. Given a full-support initial reproduction pmf $q_0$, for $t=0,1,\ldots$ set
$$
Z_i(q_t)=\sum_{j=1}^n q_t(j)e^{-\beta d_{ij}},\qquad W_t(j\mid i)=\frac{q_t(j)e^{-\beta d_{ij}}}{Z_i(q_t)},\qquad q_{t+1}(j)=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iW_t(j\mid i).
$$
All denominators are positive, every row of $W_t$ sums to one, and $q_{t+1}$ has full support. Define the nats objective $L_\beta(W)=I_{\rm nat}(X;\widehat X)+\beta\mathbb E d(X,\widehat X)$, the current channel value $L_t=L_\beta(W_t)$, and the a-posteriori factor
$$
\gamma_t:=\max_{1\le j\le n}\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\frac{e^{-\beta d_{ij}}}{Z_i(q_t)}\ge1.
$$
The certified stopping rule for tolerance $\tau>0$ is to stop when a rigorous upper interval bound on $\ln\gamma_t$ is at most $\tau$; the certificate theorem proves $L_t-L_\beta^*\le\ln\gamma_t$. When $p_i,d_{ij},\beta$ are rational inputs, outward-rounded interval evaluation of the finite formulas and exponentials supplies such bounds. The displayed iteration is the exact-real mathematical recurrence; no bit-complexity bound is asserted.
lem-it-stationary-block-rdf-limit-and-en:
## Statement

For a stationary finite-alphabet source and bounded additive distortion as in [[def-it-stationary-finite-block-information-rdf]], the sequence $R_n(D)$ has a limit for every feasible $D$, and
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}R_n(D)=\inf_{n\ge1}R_n(D)=R_{\rm block}(D).
$$
The function $R_{\rm block}$ is nonincreasing and convex on $[D_{\min},\infty)$, is zero for $D\ge D_{\rm c}$, and is right-continuous at $D_{\min}$. It is infinite below $D_{\min}$.
thm-it-finite-alphabet-rate-distortion-c:
## Statement

Let $(X_i)_{i\ge0}$ be iid with a pmf on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be finite nonnegative distortion. For every $D\ge0$, the expected-distortion and positive-slack excess-distortion operational rates of [[def-it-operational-rate-distortion-function]] both equal the finite information rate-distortion function of [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]], with value $+\infty$ when $D<D_{\min}$.
thm-it-gaussian-squared-error-rate-disto:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $X\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, where $\sigma^2\ge0$, and let squared error $d(x,y)=(x-y)^2$ be used in the standard-Borel information rate-distortion function [[def-it-general-rate-distortion-function]]. For $D\ge0$, if $\sigma^2>0$, then
$$
R(D)=\begin{cases}+\infty,&D=0,\\[2pt]\frac12\log_2^+(\sigma^2/D),&D>0,\end{cases}
$$
where $\log_2^+(u)=\max(0,\log_2u)$. If $\sigma^2=0$, then $R(D)=0$ for every $D\ge0$.
thm-it-gaussian-vector-squared-error-rat:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $m\ge1$, let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_m)$ have independent coordinates $X_i\sim N(0,\lambda_i)$ with $\lambda_i\ge0$, and let $Y\in\mathbb R^m$ be any jointly distributed reconstruction. Use squared Euclidean distortion $\mathbb E\|X-Y\|_2^2$. For $D\ge0$, the standard-Borel information rate-distortion function of [[def-it-general-rate-distortion-function]] in bits is
$$
R(D)=\begin{cases}+\infty,&D=0<\sum_i\lambda_i,\\[2pt] \frac12\sum_{i=1}^m\log_2^+(\lambda_i/\theta),&0<D<\sum_i\lambda_i,\\[2pt] 0,&D\ge\sum_i\lambda_i, \end{cases}
$$
where in the middle case $\theta$ is the unique positive solution of $\sum_i\min(\lambda_i,\theta)=D$. If all $\lambda_i=0$, then $R(D)=0$ for every $D\ge0$.
lem-it-random-cut-ergodic-block-channel-:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a stationary ergodic source on a finite alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be bounded. For any feasible $D\ge D_{\min}$ and any $r>R_{\rm block}(D)$, there is a jointly stationary ergodic pair $(X_t,\widehat X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ with the given source marginal, $\mathbb E d(X_0,\widehat X_0)\le D$, and
$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n I(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})<r.
$$
thm-it-blahut-arimoto-certified-gap-term:
## Statement

For the iteration of [[alg-it-finite-alphabet-blahut-arimoto]], let $L_\beta^*$ be the minimum of $I_{\rm nat}(X;\widehat X)+\beta\mathbb E d$ over all finite test channels. For every minimizer's output law $q^*$, every integer $t\ge0$, and full-support initialization $q_0$,
$$
0\le L_t-L_\beta^*\le\frac{D(q^*\|q_0)}{t+1}.
$$
For uniform $q_0$, this is at most $\ln n/(t+1)$. At every iteration the a-posteriori bound $L_t-L_\beta^*\le\ln\gamma_t$ holds; moreover $\gamma_t\to1$, so every positive tolerance in the algorithm's stopping rule is eventually certified, including when all minimizers lie on the boundary of the reproduction simplex.
thm-it-stationary-ergodic-rate-distortio:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a stationary ergodic finite-alphabet source, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be bounded. With the positive-slack operational definitions of [[def-it-operational-rate-distortion-function]] and the stationary quantities of [[def-it-stationary-finite-block-information-rdf]], for every $D\ge D_{\min}$,
$$
R_{\rm op}^{\rm avg}(D)=R_{\rm op}^{\rm slack}(D)=R_{\rm block}(D)=R_{\rm erg}(D).
$$
All four quantities are $+\infty$ for $D<D_{\min}$. At $D=D_{\min}$, no assertion is made for the stricter exact-threshold requirement $\mathbb P(d_n>D)\to0$.
ex-it-binary-hamming-rate-distortion-cur:
## Statement

For a Bernoulli-$1/4$ source with Hamming distortion, the rates at $D=0,1/8,1/4$ are respectively $h_2(1/4)$, $h_2(1/4)-h_2(1/8)$, and $0$. At $D=1/8$, the backward test-channel reproduction mass is $P(\widehat X=1)=1/6$; at $D=1/4$, a constant zero reproduction attains rate zero. The rate tends continuously to zero as $D\uparrow1/4$.
cex-it-continuous-optimal-reconstruction:
## Statement

Let $X\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma^2>0$, use squared-error distortion, and choose $D\ge\sigma^2$. The constant reconstruction $Y=0$ attains the Gaussian information rate-distortion value zero, but its law $\delta_0$ has no density with respect to Lebesgue measure.
ex-it-gaussian-distortion-waterline:
## Statement

Let $X_1\sim N(0,4)$ and $X_2\sim N(0,1)$ be independent, and use total squared-error budget $D=5/2$. The water level is $\theta=3/2$, the optimal coordinate distortions are $(3/2,1)$, and the information rate is $\frac12\log_2(8/3)$ bits per vector. An attaining reconstruction is $Y_1=\sqrt{5/2}U$, $Y_2=0$, where $X_1=\sqrt{5/2}U+\sqrt{3/2}V$ for independent standard normals $U,V$.
